evaluated_queries.query_text: What are the unresolved write-back rules for Documentum and how do they impact the backfill?

blinded_evidence.title: Documentum Write-Back Rules
blinded_evidence.retrieval_text: - **Repository controls — Jack O’Shea identified unresolved write-back rules.** The business requirements still need to establish whether low-confidence fields can enter Documentum, when model output should be withheld, and how duplicate documents should be handled. Permission to delete documents is also unresolved. These questions affect changes to existing repository records, not just extraction accuracy. The immediate process concern is defining what writing back actually entails, including the testing needed to support it. [00:04:13–00:04:37; 00:17:13–00:17:52]

blinded_evidence.title: Documentum Backfill Expectations
blinded_evidence.retrieval_text: - **Documentum readiness — Jack O’Shea reset backfill expectations.** Backfill means writing properties to documents already stored in Documentum. PGD leadership had expected an imminent start, but more consistent model performance and clearer document-handling requirements are prerequisites. Jack reported that leadership understood both the progress and the remaining complexity after the preceding review. Model consistency remains an open readiness dependency; no separate remediation assignment or completion date was committed in this session. [00:03:11–00:05:01]

evaluated_queries.query_text: What are the observed delivery frictions on DocIQ and what is the plan for product-led executive communication?

blinded_evidence.title: DocIQ Scope and Accountability
blinded_evidence.retrieval_text: - **Scope and accountability — Jack O’Shea acknowledged Apex Global-driven delivery friction.** The Q2 project vision had changed substantially through Q3 and Q4, with scope creep and insufficient product direction contributing to difficulty. Jack balanced that acknowledgment with satisfaction in the team’s work. Both attendees supported product-led executive communication, with engineers providing technical context rather than carrying commitments beyond their control. The intended change concerns who leads and owns the message, while preserving useful engineering participation. [00:05:18–00:05:56; 00:09:39–00:14:40]

blinded_evidence.title: DocIQ Engineering Focus
blinded_evidence.retrieval_text: - **Engineering focus — Amit Ayer clarified the team’s broader technical strengths.** Capabilities extend beyond data work to front-end development, software engineering, extraction, embeddings, and classification. Additional technical-lead capacity and stronger product oversight are intended to reduce competing coordination demands. Both attendees connected delivery problems to optimistic planning and changing direction, rather than a lack of technical ability. Clearer requirements and earlier escalation of dependencies were the practical improvements discussed for protecting engineering delivery. [00:06:10–00:09:33; 00:13:40–00:14:40]

evaluated_queries.query_text: What is the cost of scaling DocIQ and what architectural changes were proposed to improve economics?

blinded_evidence.title: DocIQ Model Economics
blinded_evidence.retrieval_text: - **Model economics — Amit Ayer flagged the cost of scaling DocIQ.** Amit recalled model-cost figures declining from nearly $1 to approximately $0.10; the measurement basis and document volume were unspecified. These remain approximate recollections rather than a verified per-document baseline or savings calculation. He also reported greater phase-two attention to sustainable human review, retraining, confidence governance, and image caching. That design attention connects extraction performance with operating cost, while implementation and measured benefits remain unverified. [00:14:56–00:15:37]

evaluated_queries.query_text: How did Amit suggest separating the work tracks for DocIQ remediation and enhancements?

blinded_evidence.title: Work organization
blinded_evidence.retrieval_text: - **Work organization — Amit Ayer suggested separating remediation from enhancements.** His proposed Track A grouped staged backfill with DMT confidence alignment. A separate Track B grouped feature enhancements, including the file-upload interface and extraction-related work. This distinction would separate preparation for repository updates from additional functionality. The extraction detail was not developed further in the discussion. These were advisory work-track suggestions; no revised work breakdown, delivery assignment, or release commitment was adopted. [00:16:15–00:16:35]

evaluated_queries.query_text: What pilot size was suggested for backfill validation and what were the proposed measurements?

blinded_evidence.title: Backfill validation
blinded_evidence.retrieval_text: - **Backfill validation — Amit Ayer suggested an optional 5,000-document pilot.** Rather than an all-or-nothing backfill, he described smaller pilot batches and offered 5,000 documents through the validation interface as one possibility. The proposed measurements were error calibration and throughput, giving leadership evidence about processing behavior while limiting operational exposure. The number was an example, not an agreed batch size. No pilot execution commitment, acceptance criteria, or measured results were established. [00:16:40–00:17:02]

evaluated_queries.query_text: What confidence routing thresholds were proposed for automatic document handling versus human triage?

blinded_evidence.title: Confidence routing
blinded_evidence.retrieval_text: - **Confidence routing — Amit Ayer suggested automatic handling above a proposed floor.** His advisory example used “Above 90” for automatic handling and lower-confidence results going to the validation interface for human triage, potentially through different queues. The number’s unit was unspecified, and behavior at exactly 90 was not defined. This remained a suggested routing concept rather than an approved threshold or implemented control; the business requirements for write-back remained open. [00:17:56–00:18:12]

evaluated_queries.query_text: Why was there frustration expressed regarding parallel document-processing initiatives like LENS?

blinded_evidence.retrieval_text: - **Portfolio overlap — Jack O’Shea reported frustration with DocIQ-like initiatives.** Jack described parallel document-processing efforts elsewhere in the company as frustrating. Amit’s LENS experience concerned confidence metrics and additional data. The substantive question is how the initiatives fit together; consolidation, shared architecture, and changes to project charters remain open. [00:18:27–00:19:39]
